blockingIssues: 04-1042-handoff-desktop.png and 04-1042-read-desktop.png: the narrative beat paragraph is truncated by the bottom of the pinned 1440x900 viewport, so its final line is unreachable. In the handoff frame the last text pixels sit at row 898 of 899 (bottom margin 2px) and the visible text ends mid-clause on a trailing comma: 'berulang kali menjadi batas, jalur,'. The missing continuation is 'benteng, jembatan, dan saksi.' — confirmed present in 04-1042-nomenclature-check.png, so the copy exists and is simply pushed off-screen. The read frame is worse: only 2 of the 4 lines are visible and the third is sliced mid-glyph at row 899. Because the scene is pinned, no further scrolling reveals it — scrolling advances the beat timeline instead. This is a regression: round 4's own record measured this same paragraph completing at y=845 of 900, i.e. it fit before this round's content top-padding change and does not now.

02-921-handoff-desktop.png and 02-921-read-desktop.png: the same bottom-of-pin truncation. At handoff the beat block ends at row 893 of 899 (bottom margin 6px) showing only 'Dan ketika sebuah tempat memiliki / nama, ia mulai memperoleh' — a transitive clause left without its object. The missing line 'identitas yang dapat diwariskan' is confirmed in 02-921-nomenclature-check.png. In the read frame the second line is cut mid-glyph at row 899. This coincides with this round's column narrowing: the master line now sets as six near-single-word lines ('Kadhiri. / Sebuah / nama / muncul / dari dalam / sejarah.') running to y=673. The beats sit about 155px below the master line's end, so flow height alone does not fully account for the position and a shared padding change may also contribute — the exact mechanism is proven only for 1042, but the truncation itself is measured on both.

Cross-scene inconsistency confirming the above is layout, not capture timing: measured at the handoff (near-transition) state, the beat block's bottom margin is 98px on 01-879, 112px on 03-1015 and 22px on 00-prologue — all with complete, terminally punctuated sentences — versus 6px on 02-921 and 2px on 04-1042, both with unfinished sentences. On the two failing scenes the block's bottom edge barely moves across a full scroll state (899 to 893 on 921, 899 to 897 on 1042, i.e. 6px and 2px), so the overflow is a settled position rather than a mid-entrance frame, while 879 and 1015 at that same state show the identical component settled with roughly 100px of air. Two of five scenes therefore lose narrative copy on desktop while the other three do not.
notes: Both round-4 defects named in the brief are genuinely fixed and I verified each by pixel measurement. On 04-1042 the hatched handoff rule now sits at y=87-118 (read) / ~y=100-110 (handoff), clearing the nav chrome by roughly 30-45px and the top of the '1042' numerals (y=192 read, y=165 handoff) by 60-74px; it no longer touches the date or the master line's first sentence. On 02-921 the master line's last line 'sejarah.' occupies y=612-669, entirely below the 'K A D H I R I' band at y=504-565 — zero vertical overlap — and the nearest horizontal approach is 'dari dalam' ending at x=382 against the 'K' at x=504, a 122px gap versus 18-28px of internal letterspacing inside KADHIRI. That is a decisive fix, not a marginal one. Scope caveat: the capture set contains only 1440x900 and 390x844, so the 1024x768 laptop breakpoint the brief says was also measured is unverified by this review.

The analogous pairing on 04-1042 is also safe: 'air suci.' ends at x=299 and 'PANJALU' begins at x=375, a 76px gap against 7-13px of internal letterspacing in PANJALU. The two runs read as separate elements despite sharing a baseline band.

The mobile reduced-motion fallback is the strongest part of this build and I found nothing wrong with it: clean vertical stacks (image, date, gold rule, master line, then beats in legible scrim panels), the complete narrative present with no truncation, and the decorative name labels (KADHIRI; PANJALU/JANGGALA/BRANTAS) correctly sitting below the beats with clear separation in the two nomenclature-check captures. Ironically the mobile frames are what prove the desktop copy loss, since they carry the exact lines the pinned desktop scenes cut off.

Minor, non-blocking: in 02-921-nomenclature-check.png the small square beat-marker sits flush against the final 'n' of 'diwariskan' with zero gap, while the identical marker on 04-1042-nomenclature-check.png has roughly 90px of clearance after 'saksi.'. Legibility survives — the marker abuts the letterform rather than overprinting it — but the spacing is inconsistent between scenes.

All five establish frames are deliberately textless: each measures an identical 28 body pixels above luminance 200, i.e. header chrome only. Read as a consistent establishing-shot rhythm this works, and 01-879 and 03-1015 are exemplary complete frames — big date, master line, two fully legible beats over scrim, roughly 100px of bottom air. Those two scenes are exactly what the other three should match.
